This ZIP defines the service flag
for the Zcash peer-to-peer protocol specified in ZIP 204
. A node that sets it serves at least the most recent 2,304 blocks of its best chain, but not necessarily older blocks. It is the Zcash counterpart of BIP 159
A node that deletes old block bodies, such as a Zebra node with pruning enabled, cannot set
, and ZIP 204 defines no other flag for serving blocks. Peers cannot tell that such a node serves recent blocks: some ignore it, and others request historical blocks it does not have.

A limited peer SHOULD NOT serve blocks more than 2,304 blocks below its best tip. It MAY disconnect a peer that requests a block more than 2,306 blocks below its best tip; the 2-block margin allows for the best tip advancing while a request is in flight.

A node MUST NOT request a block from a limited peer if that block is more than 2,304 blocks below the node’s own best tip. A node SHOULD rely on limited peers for blocks only while its best tip is within 1,152 blocks of the network’s best tip, leaving half of the window for chain reorganizations and for differences between the two nodes’ best tips.
This ZIP requires no network upgrade. Nodes ignore service flags they do not recognize, so a node can set
as soon as it implements this ZIP.
Bit 10 and the 2,304-block window match the Version 2 P2P protocol draft
, so a node can advertise the same capability in both protocols. Bit 10 is also the bit that BIP 159 assigns to the same capability in Bitcoin.

The window is defined in blocks rather than time, so that a peer can check a request against it without knowing the block target spacing. At 75, 25 and 10 seconds per block it covers about 48, 16 and 6.4 hours.

The 1,152-block margin for requesters, and the rule against serving older blocks, follow BIP 159’s 144-block reorganization buffer and its fingerprinting countermeasure. BIP 159 does not specify disconnection; the 2-block margin follows Bitcoin Core’s implementation
A limited peer that served every block it retains would reveal its retention depth, which helps distinguish it from other nodes. Serving only the window avoids this.
